name: rect_no_transform_control
_comment: The control: no element transform and no layer transform, so the evaluated bbox must equal the plain geometric bbox. Separates a runner that mis-builds the document or applies a stray matrix; it does NOT separate a port that ignores transforms (nothing to ignore), which is why the eight vectors below exist.

name: rect_translate
_comment: translate(100,50). A port that ignores the element transform returns [0,0,10,10].

name: rect_scale_nonuniform
_comment: scale(2,3) about the document origin on a rect at (5,10), so the ORIGIN moves too: [10,30,20,30]. A port that scales the size but leaves the position returns [5,10,20,30]; one that ignores the transform returns [5,10,10,10].

name: rect_rotate_45
_comment: rotate(45 degrees) about the origin of a 10x10 rect at the origin: the AABB is the square's diagonal, 10*sqrt(2) on a side, spanning x in [-5*sqrt(2), 5*sqrt(2)] and y in [0, 10*sqrt(2)]. Chosen because the answer is NOT axis-aligned-invariant: swapping b and c (the classic wrong-space slip, i.e. rotating by -45) returns [0,-7.0710678118654755,14.142135623730951,14.142135623730951] - the same extent, transposed. Ignoring the transform returns [0,0,10,10].

name: rect_skew_x
_comment: skewX with c = 0.5: x' = x + 0.5*y, so the 10x10 rect shears to a 15-wide, 10-tall AABB. Swapping b and c (skewY instead) returns [0,0,10,15] - the transpose, which is why width and height differ here.

name: rect_composed_matrix
_comment: A general matrix with every entry live (a=2 b=1 c=-0.5 d=1.5 e=7 f=-3) on a 4x6 rect at (1,2). Corners map to (8,1) (16,5) (13,14) (5,10), so the AABB is [5,1,11,13] - all four values differ from the untransformed [1,2,4,6], and swapping b and c gives [11,-2.5,14,11].

name: rect_layer_transform_only
_comment: The ANCESTOR leg: the element carries no transform and the containing layer carries translate(20,30). A port that folds only the element's own matrix returns [0,0,10,10].

name: rect_element_then_layer_order
_comment: COMPOSITION ORDER, the one thing a commuting pair cannot pin: the element scales 2x and the layer translates (5,5). Innermost-first (correct) maps (10,10) to (20,20) then to (25,25), giving [5,5,20,20]; outermost-first would give [10,10,20,20]. Same two matrices, different answer - so this vector is what separates the order.

name: rect_stroked_uses_geometric_bounds
_comment: The evaluated bbox is built from GEOMETRIC bounds, so a 4-wide stroke must NOT inflate it: [0,0,10,10], not the preview bbox [-2,-2,14,14]. The transform is the identity here so the vector isolates that one choice.
